notes: §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR1 (added by Amendment 1): "Argument-1 must be an identifier, a literal, or an arithmetic expression. Specific rules governing the number, class, and category of argument-1 are given in the definition of each function." The grammar rule functionArgument reads a nonnumeric literal or an arithmetic expression (an identifier and a numeric literal are its sole-operand cases) and BindArgOperandCore binds each as the kind it was written: a literal operand, a field operand, or a computed operand whose identifiers must be numeric (COBOL0844). The arms a later edition added to that rule are each refused at 85: the boolean expression of §2023:8.4.3.2.3 SR8 by VisitFunctionArgument (COBOL0900), ADDRESS OF by VisitAddressIdentifier, a national or boolean literal by VisitNonNumericLiteral, OMITTED and a phrase word by BindArgOperandCore (COBOL1544, COBOL1638). The second sentence is BindFunctionResult, which counts the arguments against the catalog row TryGet returns (COBOL1504), and CheckArgumentClasses, which asks the per-position class rules of Verified (COBOL1627); neither has an edition arm. Probed at --std 85: accepted with the right value are an elementary, group, qualified, subscripted and reference-modified item, a function-identifier as an argument, nonnumeric and numeric literals (signed, decimal, comma and semicolon separators), the figurative constants SPACE, QUOTE, ZERO, HIGH-VALUE, ALL literal and a symbolic-character, and expressions with every operator, a unary sign, parentheses and a nested function; refused are a relation, a condition-name, an index-name, a file-name, a paragraph-name, a mnemonic-name, an undefined name, OMITTED, LEADING and TRAILING, ADDRESS OF, a boolean expression, B, N and X literals, a concatenation, the PHYSICAL, LOCALE and ANYCASE phrases, a wrong count for MOD, SQRT, CURRENT-DATE, WHEN-COMPILED, UPPER-CASE, MAX, RANDOM, ANNUITY, PRESENT-VALUE and ORD, and a wrong class for UPPER-CASE, LOWER-CASE, REVERSE, NUMVAL, SQRT, MAX, LENGTH, CHAR, ORD, FACTORIAL, INTEGER-OF-DATE, DATE-OF-INTEGER, MEAN, SUM, RANDOM, MOD and REM. The empty list FUNCTION RANDOM () is accepted at 85; that is the general format's braces, the row 1985-FMT-IV.4.3.8.3.2, not this rule. The witness runs UPPER-CASE over an item and a literal and MAX over an expression and an item.

next.reason: §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR1 (added by Amendment 1, X3.23a-1989; Errata C95): "Argument-1 must be an identifier, a literal, or an arithmetic expression. Specific rules governing the number, class, and category of argument-1 are given in the definition of each function." §2023:8.4.3.2.3 SR8: "Argument-1 shall be an identifier, a literal, a boolean expression, or an arithmetic expression. Specific rules governing the number, class, category, and type of argument-1 are given for intrinsic functions in the definition of that intrinsic function in Clause 15 ... and for user-defined functions in 14.8.2, Parameters and 14.8.3, Returning items." The words that differ: "a boolean expression", a fourth kind of argument that 1985 refuses; "and type"; and the second source of the specific rules, "for user-defined functions". The three 1985 kinds of argument are kept.
